seo.title: Homeless help in Leeds - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Leeds: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, application, referral or outreach contact does not guarantee accommodation or another service. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.

content.text: Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.

if you have nowhere safe tonight, call Housing Options and say clearly that you are homeless today. If you may lose your home within 56 days, ask for prevention help now. The published assessment wait can be up to four weeks for non-emergencies, so explain any same-day risk clearly.

Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
Merrion House, 110 Merrion Centre, Leeds LS2 8BB

Open Monday 9am–4pm, Tuesday 10am–4pm and Wednesday–Friday 9am–4pm. Call or attend if you have nowhere tonight. Email if homelessness is likely within 56 days; replies are normally within three working days. Ask to make a homeless application and explain all risks. Emergency or temporary accommodation depends on an assessment.
3rd Floor, Duncan House, 14 Duncan Street, Leeds LS1 6DL

Give an exact public sleeping location, usual time and description. The team can assess someone sleeping outside and connect them with emergency accommodation and other services. Contact does not guarantee that the person will be found or housed that day.

Send an alert about an adult sleeping outside when the location and time are known. StreetLink passes the information to the Leeds outreach team; it is not an emergency service or a bed-booking service. Call 999 for urgent medical danger or a child under 18 who is at risk.

Independent outreach and emotional and practical support for people who may not be engaging with other services. It does not provide emergency accommodation. Use Housing Options or Street Outreach for a same-day housing need.
Call 999 in immediate danger. For emergency housing call Housing Options on
outside hours. Do not return for papers or belongings if it is unsafe.

categories.title: 2. Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

content.text: The Care Centre offers meals, showers, clothing and support. Its emergency accommodation is accessed by referral through Leeds Housing Options on
; it is not a guaranteed walk-in bed.

For adults aged 18+ who are homeless or vulnerably housed. Services include showers, laundry, a safe mail address, housing and benefits support, referrals, and free employment, training, life-skills and English-language classes. Ask what is available that day.
Search by need and location for current accommodation advice, meals, health care, practical help and specialist services. Details can change, so confirm with the provider before a long journey.
Search accommodation, day centres and specialist services by location and eligibility. Confirm the referral route, vacancies, age limits and pet rules directly.
A free three-course lunch is served Monday–Friday, normally 12 noon–12:35pm. Call
before a long journey because capacity and times can change.

items.name: St Anne's breakfast and evening food

content.text: Breakfast starts at 8:30am Monday–Friday. Community groups normally provide evening food on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. Finish times and providers vary, so call
or check the live list before travelling.
Chapel FM Arts Centre, York Road, Leeds LS14 6JB
A free community meal is normally served Tuesday at 6:30pm. No booking is normally required. Meals and capacity depend on volunteers and supplies.
St Luke's Church, Malvern Road, Holbeck, Leeds LS11 8PD
A free community meal is normally served Wednesday at 6:30pm, without advance booking. Confirm the session on the current list.
Food and befriending support is normally available Saturday 11am–1pm. This is a faith-community service; check the live list before travelling.
St Aidan's Church, Elford Place West, Leeds LS8 5QD
A food parcel session is normally held Saturday 10:30am–12 noon, without referral, with one parcel per household. Stock and rules can change.

items.name: Meeting Point: refugees and asylum seekers

content.text: Christ Church, Armley Ridge Road, Leeds LS12 3LE
. Monday sessions normally run 2:15pm–5pm with a hot meal, drinks, food parcels, low-cost clothing and household items, advocacy and digital access.

A free weekly parcel is normally available Sunday 10am–12 noon in the mosque basement. The first visit requires evidence of income or benefits and identity or address, which can make this service unsuitable if documents are missing. Email

The Leeds Food Aid Network map includes meals, food parcels, pantries and referral routes. Some services accept direct attendance; others need a voucher or evidence. Check each entry before travelling.
Adults who are homeless or vulnerably housed can ask about showers, laundry, clothing and other practical support Monday–Friday 8:30am–4:30pm. Call
Ask the Care Centre about showers, clothing and practical support. Availability can depend on demand. Call

Fortnightly city-centre outreach can include hot food and drinks, hygiene and underwear packs, coats, sleeping bags and footwear. Dates and locations change; check the official events list or ask St Anne's before travelling.
or NHS 111 online. Say if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover.
. Specialist primary care for people who are homeless or unstably housed, refugees and asylum seekers, and people using substance services.
Current NHS hours are Monday 8am–6pm, Tuesday 8am–1pm and 3pm–6pm, and Wednesday–Friday 8am–6pm; the front door opens at 8:30am. Call first, especially around Tuesday's midday closure.

items.name: Register with a GP without documents

content.text: GP care is free. You do not need proof of address, immigration status, identification or an NHS number to register. If the form asks for an address, use a temporary address or ask whether the surgery address can be used.
If refused for lack of papers, ask for the refusal in writing and contact NHS England or Citizens Advice.
Call NHS 111 for urgent dental pain, swelling, bleeding or trauma. For routine care, use the NHS dentist search and contact practices directly. Availability and NHS acceptance change frequently.
and select option 2 for urgent mental-health support. Call 999 if life is in immediate danger.
for free, confidential, anonymous text support at any time; it is not an emergency service.
First-time visitors can normally turn up from 6pm. Returning visitors should call
after 6pm. Open Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 6pm–2am.
Dial House provides a non-medical safe space for people in crisis. It is not overnight accommodation.
Face-to-face emotional and practical support for people aged 16+ is normally available daily 3pm–9pm. Call or text
to check access. It is not a bed or emergency medical service.
Free, confidential advice and treatment for alcohol and drug problems. Call or use the self-referral route. Say if homelessness, withdrawal risk or medication affects safety.

categories.title: 7. Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

content.text: Municipal Buildings, Calverley Street, Leeds LS1 3AB
. Open Monday–Wednesday 9am–8pm, Thursday–Friday 9am–5pm and Saturday 10am–4pm; closed Sunday.

Free Wi-Fi, internet computers, accessible public toilets, printing and photocopying. It is free to enter and stay. Library membership is free for people who live, work or study in Leeds, and identification is not required to join.

Use the council's live map for locations and accessibility. The page states general opening of 10am–6:30pm but also says locking begins at 4pm, so arrive early and check the map. Some accessible toilets need a RADAR key, available for £2 from community hubs.

Hubs provide free computers and help with council services, benefits, debt, jobs and online tasks. City Centre Community Hub is at Merrion House, Woodhouse Lane, Leeds LS2 8LX; open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 9am–5pm and Tuesday 10am–5pm.
Libraries, community hubs and partner venues provide free, safe and warm places during the colder months. Locations and seasonal hours change; use the council list before travelling.
The council scheme may help with food or fuel, essential appliances, furniture or carpets, and some removal costs when fleeing violence. Apply online. If you cannot use the form, call
A decision is normally aimed for within four working days. Evidence, a bank statement and National Insurance number may be requested. Help is assessed and is not guaranteed immediate cash.

items.name: Universal Credit without a fixed address

content.text: You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack identification, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.

Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether the claimant commitment should change temporarily. In some supported or temporary accommodation, Housing Benefit may cover rent separately.
Universal Credit guidance for homeless people
Free benefit checks, claims, form filling, challenges and appeals. Deaf or hard-of-hearing people can text

content.text: Oxford House, Oxford Row, Leeds LS1 3BE
, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. A Wednesday drop-in is normally open 9am–1pm, but check before attending.
Free advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment and other problems. Take letters or notices if available, but ask for help even when documents are missing.

categories.title: 9. Work, training and travel to an interview

content.text: Free drop-in help with jobs, apprenticeships, training, CVs, applications, interviews and careers. Staff may be able to help with travel to interviews. Open Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, Tuesday from 10am, without appointment. Free Wi-Fi is available.
. Ask before buying travel because support is not automatic.

items.name: St Anne's classes and Big Issue North

content.text: Ask about free employment, training, life-skills and English-language classes. Big Issue North can explain magazine selling as a legitimate income option and offer practical support; call
Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Free advice on CVs, interviews, qualifications, training and careers for adults in England. Ask for phone or online support if travel is difficult.
. Education, requalification, training, employment and integration support.

St Anne's Resource Centre may provide a safe correspondence address for adults who are homeless or vulnerably housed. Ask first about permission, the exact format, collection times and how long mail is kept.
send post or leave identification, papers or belongings at any service without explicit permission.

Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing the National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Citizens Advice or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.

items.name: Replace a birth certificate or get passport advice

content.text: Order certificates through the General Register Office or relevant register office; fees apply. Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help with an application but cannot guarantee the fee.

Leeds Central Library and community hubs provide free internet access; printing may cost. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found. Ask a housing or day-centre worker about safe options before leaving anything.

, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Free advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment and some immigration issues.
Do not miss a deadline or court hearing while waiting for advice. Take notices and court papers if you have them.
Free, confidential advice on homelessness, possession, tenancy rights, repairs and housing problems. Appointments are required.

If facing possession, attend the hearing and ask court staff for the free Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service. Do not wait for another appointment and miss court.
Unit 24, UNITY Business Centre, 26 Roundhay Road, Leeds LS7 1AB

categories.title: 13. Domestic abuse, young people, LGBTQ+ people, veterans, older and disabled people

content.text: Support for people of all genders, families and children, including drop-ins, specialist advocacy, safety, housing and welfare help. Emergency accommodation and refuge are subject to assessment and availability; a women-only refuge is available. Ask for an interpreter if needed.
Housing Options has specific help for people aged 16–21. State your age immediately. If under 18, call Children's Services on
outside hours. Call 999 if in danger.
People aged 16–25 can also call Centrepoint on
, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, for advice. Sofa surfing still counts as homelessness.
Contact your personal adviser and Housing Options. Tell both services you are a care leaver and whether accommodation will end today.
3 Park Court, 40 Park Cross Street, Leeds LS1 2QH
LGBTQ+ health and wellbeing, sexual health, counselling, groups and trans support. It is not emergency accommodation.

For women, including trans women, who live or work in Leeds and are involved in sex work. Health, safety, housing, welfare, domestic- and sexual-violence, and work or exit support.
. Any veteran who is homeless or at risk can self-refer for housing and tenancy support through the national pathway. Accommodation is individually assessed.
The Leeds Veterans and Families Hub can also connect people with local housing, health, employment and financial support.
Bradbury Building, Mark Lane, Leeds LS2 8JA
, Monday–Friday 10am–3pm. Free information and advice for older people on benefits, housing, health, care and local support.

Ask for a care assessment or report abuse, neglect or self-neglect affecting an adult. Reports can be anonymous. Social care does not replace a homeless application; contact both services if care needs affect safe accommodation.

Street Paws works in Leeds and Yorkshire, offering veterinary support through referral and helping services consider pet-friendly options. Ask a housing or support worker about referral. Street Paws cannot directly arrange accommodation, fostering or kennels.

People experiencing homelessness can use the UK help form to ask about volunteer veterinary support. Eligibility and local coverage are assessed. StreetVet is not an emergency service and does not cover existing bills or provide fostering.

The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.

items.name: Tell every service about your pet

content.text: Tell Housing Options and every referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Simon on the Streets reports that one Leeds hostel has two kennels, but access and availability require referral and cannot be promised.
Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting admission.
Simon on the Streets pet information
, Monday–Saturday 7am–8pm and Sunday and bank holidays 8am–8pm. Ask about routes, times, fares, accessibility and live disruption.
Ask about journey planning and ticket options. Opening times vary, so call MetroLine before travelling. No free-travel entitlement is assumed.

items.name: Travel for interviews or essential appointments

content.text: Ask a Jobshop, Jobcentre work coach, housing worker or health service before buying a ticket whether authorised travel help is available. Leeds Jobshops may help with interview travel, but approval is not automatic.

Frequent direct buses connect Leeds and the airport. Leeds is the nearest mainline railway station, with bus connections including the A1. Check the current route, first and last bus and fare before travelling; the airport is not a shelter.
Services change. Please report a closed service, wrong detail or safer alternative through the project repository. Do not send private medical, immigration or housing documents.
